papers.title: AIM-STAGE: a self-supervised framework via adaptive interval-aware multi-kernel calibration and spectro-temporal exploration for few-shot EEG staging.
papers.summary: Proposes AIM-STAGE, a self-supervised representation learning framework combining STFT spectro-temporal exploration, a CNN-Transformer encoder, and adaptive interval-aware multi-kernel calibration for few-shot EEG sleep staging. It improved accuracy from 88.67% to 92.04% on SLEEP-2013 and outperformed six baselines on all four datasets (kappa, macro-F1, balanced accuracy), with N1 remaining the hardest stage (F1 0.003-0.046).

papers.title: Anti-correlation time-frequency synergy and dual-granularity fusion for sleep stage classification.
papers.summary: Develops a single-channel EEG sleep staging network using a multi-branch module for anti-correlated frequency features, dual-granularity residual attention fusion, causal transition-aware learning, and focal loss. It reached overall accuracies of 87.0%, 83.4%, and 84.5% on SleepEDF-20, SleepEDF-78, and SHHS, respectively, including N1 accuracies of 57.5%, 52.5%, and 49.3%.

papers.title: Thalamic stereo-EEG detects sleep stages N2 and N3 with discrimination approaching scalp EEG
papers.summary: Analyzed 477 h of simultaneous stereo-EEG and scalp EEG from six adults to test whether thalamic channels identify N2+N3 sleep better than other intracranial sites, using a random forest with HMM decoding and the pretrained SleepSEEG classifier. Thalamic channels performed best among regions sampled in all participants (AUC 0.94 with RF+HMM and 0.93 with SleepSEEG), supporting thalamic N2+N3 detection for sleep-targeted neuromodulation.

papers.title: Dynamics of Sleep Architecture and Nocturnal Oxygen Saturation During Acclimatization at Intermediate Altitude: A Longitudinal Observational Study in Elite Athletes.
papers.summary: Longitudinally tracked nocturnal sleep architecture and oxygen saturation with wearable EEG and ring oximetry in 17 elite athletes across a 2-week intermediate-altitude training camp (2100 m). Over the first week %N3 decreased and %REM increased logarithmically, with sleep-stage-specific SpO2 recovery and heart-rate dynamics indicating non-uniform acclimatization across sleep stages.

papers.title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
papers.summary: Presents the Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model for real-time EEG phase estimation on theta-band stimulus-aligned and alpha-band resting-state signals, benchmarked against DBCNN, EPN, Phastimate, and PEAP. Under matched testing conditions BOB matched or exceeded these deep learning models while requiring a fraction of the calibration time.

papers.title: NeuralFieldManifold: Uncovering the Manifold Geometry of Local Field Potentials
papers.summary: Analytically and empirically shows that lag-embedded local field potential dynamics lie on a low-dimensional K-torus, with each sustained oscillatory mode contributing an independent circular degree of freedom while aperiodic 1/f structure and noise add only geometric thickness. The authors introduce DeepLagField, a physics-informed network for nonstationary recordings, and report persistent homology signatures consistent with predicted toroidal Betti numbers in primate V1, rodent hippocampal, and mouse cortical EEG data, with decoding performance rivaling conventional spectral features.

papers.title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Sleep: Integrating Multichannel Signals for Comprehensive Assessment.
papers.summary: This review examines five frontiers of multimodal AI in sleep medicine: foundation models for biosignal analysis, automated sleep staging matching expert reliability, AI-driven respiratory analysis for endotype-level characterization, AI-derived sleep biomarkers from EEG microstructure and brain age, and integration challenges. It emphasizes the potential of deep learning to enable scalable, reproducible polysomnographic analysis.

papers.title: A Lightweight EEG-Based Alzheimer's Disease Detection Framework on an Edge-Computing Platform Toward Future Intelligent Digital Twin Systems.
papers.summary: The authors propose a lightweight dilated hybrid deep learning framework with channel selection for EEG-based Alzheimer's disease detection on edge-computing platforms. It achieved 92.56% accuracy on a closed-eye dataset and 75.15% on an open-eye dataset, with inference times of 10.45 ms and 8.23 ms per segment and energy consumption of 9.69 mJ and 6.95 mJ, respectively, demonstrating feasibility for real-time on-edge AD detection.

papers.title: Automated Sleep Staging: Are Algorithms Ready for the Clinic?
papers.summary: This review discusses the development and clinical implementation of AI-based automated sleep staging programs, noting their potential to improve efficiency and standardization but warning that models trained on non-heterogeneous data may yield unreliable results. It stresses the need to recognize limitations before integrating AI scoring into clinical workflows.

papers.title: SafeLens: A Statistically Controlled Nonlinear Machine Learning Framework for Characterizing Hidden Dynamics in Event-Locked Neural Activity
papers.summary: The authors introduce SafeLens, a nonlinear machine learning framework combining random forests with empirical null sampling to statistically control false positives when characterizing event-locked neural activity. In simulated corticocortical evoked potentials injected into intracranial EEG, SafeLens recovered ~2.5 times as many polarity-resolved deflections as trial-average thresholding and the closest data-driven method, with ~5-11 times fewer false components, and in eight patients detected CCEPs above chance until 1,040 ms after stimulation versus 570 and 455 ms for benchmarks.

papers.title: Characterising cortical perturbation-recovery dynamics using TMS-EEG: The Brain Dynamic Toolbox
papers.summary: The study adapted dynamical measures from computational perturbation models to TMS-EEG data and applied them to analyze cortical perturbation-recovery dynamics in 16 healthy adults during long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI). It found that LICI altered the temporal evolution of dynamical measures: Perturbative Integration Latency Index distinguished conditions in the earliest post-stimulation window, Autocorrelation Function Width differences persisted across a broader early interval, and Lyapunov Exponent showed weaker discrimination, demonstrating that extended post-stimulation trajectories reveal additional features of cortical resilience and temporal memory.

papers.title: Slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut signals during sleep: an exploratory multivariate transfer entropy study.
papers.summary: Using overnight EEG, ECG, and bowel sound recordings from 24 healthy subjects, the study applied multivariate transfer entropy to quantify directed slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut across sleep stages. Information flow from heart to brain, brain to gut, and heart to gut consistently exceeded reverse directions, with sleep-stage-dependent dissociation of within- versus inter-system flow, presented as exploratory statistical patterns.

papers.title: Sleep and Neurodegeneration: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Early Detection and Personalized Care.
papers.summary: This review examines evidence linking sleep disturbances, neurodegeneration, and artificial intelligence, covering the glymphatic system as a mechanistic basis for bidirectional sleep-proteinopathy relationships and AI applications such as automated sleep staging, wearable monitoring, and digital therapeutics for early detection and personalized care.

papers.title: Dissociable Oscillatory Alpha and Aperiodic Neural Dynamics Underlie Atypical Attentional Control in Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
papers.summary: EEG from 45 children with ADHD and 45 typically developing children during a visual detection task was parameterized into oscillatory alpha and aperiodic components. Demand-related attentional differences appeared only in oscillatory alpha, whereas distractor-related abnormalities were reflected in the aperiodic slope, and multivariate machine learning classification based on these signatures robustly discriminated ADHD from controls.

papers.title: Clinical Validation of the New EEG Trend, Brain State of the Newborn, Against aEEG Interpretation.
papers.summary: Validated the automatically computed Brain State of the Newborn (BSN) EEG trend against expert visual aEEG interpretation in 731 epochs from 85 hypothermia-treated asphyxiated infants, finding BSN robustly differentiated aEEG background scores and correlated with recovery to continuous normal voltage (ρ=0.72). Concludes BSN offers a real-time automated complement to aEEG for assessing electrocortical recovery.

papers.title: Pediatric Sleep Medicine: Tailoring Artificial Intelligence Solutions for the Youngest Patients.
papers.summary: This review summarizes evidence for AI-assisted pediatric sleep medicine, including obstructive sleep apnea screening and severity estimation, automated sleep staging, and analysis of actigraphy and wearable signals. It emphasizes that age-specific training and validation are needed because sleep physiology and monitoring tolerance change across development.

papers.title: False-Positive Calls of Reimplemented Published Analyses for Covert Command-Following on Electroencephalograms Recorded Without Study Commands
papers.summary: Reimplemented 11 published EEG analyses for covert command-following on recordings made without commands and found that three (Goldfine 2011, du Bois 2026, Guger 2018) falsely called significantly more than 5% positive, up to 27.3% after cardiac arrest, while still detecting genuine responses. The authors argue that any positive call rule must report its false-call rate and detection at that rate.

papers.title: EEG emotion-recognition datasets for neuroarchitecture: an appraisal of openness, AI-readiness and ontology maturity.
papers.summary: Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review appraised 27 publicly obtainable EEG emotion-recognition datasets using a 52-criterion codebook across openness (FAIR), AI-readiness, and ontology maturity; none were designed for spatial neuroarchitecture research. Openness was weakest for Interoperability (2.044 vs FAIR composite 2.857), only 8 datasets were fully open, and ontology levels clustered at Level 3 with none at Levels 4-5.

papers.title: Mapping brain networks underlying abstract perceptual decision formation and its EEG signatures
papers.summary: Combining fMRI and EEG in a supramodal change-detection paradigm with individualized finite element head modeling, the study identified a decision-related network including parietal-opercular regions as dominant contributors to the centroparietal positivity (CPP) during abstract perceptual decisions.

papers.title: An Eyewear-Based EEG Interface for Temporal-Region Monitoring and Emotion Recognition
papers.summary: The authors developed an eyewear-based EEG system with dry titanium electrodes near T7/T8 and evaluated it across 103 recordings in five paradigms, retaining 93.2-100.0% of epochs after quality control. Emotion decoding yielded balanced accuracies of 0.882 (two-class) and 0.667 (three-class), and the system outperformed the Muse headband in group-held-out classification.

papers.title: Repeated prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation improves behavioral regulation and modulates resting-state EEG microstate dynamics in young adults with problematic smartphone use: a randomized sham-controlled longitudinal study.
papers.summary: Randomized 80 young adults with problematic smartphone use to active or sham left-DLPFC tDCS (2.0 mA, 12 weeks) and examined behavioral and resting-state EEG microstate outcomes. Active tDCS reduced objectively measured smartphone use, craving, and functional impairment and selectively altered microstate dynamics (e.g., decreased microstate C and increased D eyes-closed), without changes in global explained variance.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates TNBS-induced visceral pain and modulates cortical EEG rhythms in association with TREM1/DAP12 pathway inhibition: Enhanced effects with pharmacological TREM1 blockade.
papers.summary: In TNBS-induced visceral pain rats, electroacupuncture alleviated hyperalgesia and normalized cortical delta/theta EEG dysrhythmia in association with suppression of microglial TREM1/DAP12 neuroinflammation; pharmacological TREM1 blockade mimicked and enhanced these effects.

papers.title: Multiscale Neurodynamic Alterations in Major Depressive Disorder Revealed by Lempel-Ziv Complexity of Multi-Paradigm Resting-State EEG.
papers.summary: Using multiscale Lempel-Ziv complexity, the authors compared resting-state EEG multiscale dynamics between patients with major depressive disorder and healthy controls, deriving Scale-Dependent Variation Slope and Cross-Scale Correlation Coefficient features. Patients showed impaired complexity transitions from low to high frequencies and disrupted delta-centered cross-scale integration, with classification reaching a maximum accuracy of 85.71%.

papers.title: Clip-to-trial: EEG-based decoding network with long short-term self-attention for DRDS recognition.
papers.summary: The authors propose a clip-to-trial long short-term self-attention network (C2T-LSTSA) for EEG-based dynamic random-dot stereogram (DRDS) recognition, using multi-scale local feature extraction, trial-level feature reconstruction, and long short-term self-attention. On three EEG datasets from strabismus patients, it consistently outperformed state-of-the-art methods under subject-dependent and subject-independent protocols.

papers.title: Intraoperative electroencephalography burst suppression during endoscopic third ventriculostomy: Case report and implications for neuromonitoring.
papers.summary: Reported a case of a 28-year-old woman undergoing endoscopic third ventriculostomy who developed intraoperative hemodynamic crises coinciding with bilateral EEG burst suppression, which resolved slower than hemodynamics. Suggests processed intraoperative EEG may serve as an early sign of acute cerebral disturbance, though its added value remains unproven.

papers.title: Nociceptive-evoked electroencephalography can predict inter-individual differences in high frequency induced sensitisation of central nociceptive pathways: A test-retest reliability study
papers.summary: Applied high-frequency stimulation (HFS) across two identical sessions to assess test-retest reliability of pinprick- and electrically evoked EEG features and their relation to individual differences in hyperalgesia development. Reliability was poor-to-moderate and worsened for post-HFS change measures, though contralateral alpha-ERD was strengthened post-HFS and baseline alpha-ERD related to the subsequent time course of secondary hyperalgesia, while vertex potential magnitude tracked general pain intensity.

papers.title: Cannabidiol and fronto-parietal EEG connectivity in autistic children.
papers.summary: In a double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial, 12 weeks of oral cannabidiol increased beta-band resting-state EEG functional connectivity between right frontal and right inferior-parietal electrodes (F4-P8) in autistic children, with no comparable change after placebo. The authors report this as preliminary evidence requiring replication in larger samples.

papers.title: Unexplained neurological deterioration after acute brain injury: A structured intensive care framework for targeted continuous electroencephalogram.
papers.summary: Presented a narrative review and structured intensive care framework for evaluating unexplained neurological deterioration after acute brain injury, defining when targeted continuous EEG is most informative. Emphasizes that cEEG should complement, not replace, clinical examination, neuroimaging, and correction of systemic physiology.

papers.title: E2I-Flow: EEG-to-Image Reconstruction via Wavelet-Temporal Cross-Attention and Conditional Flow Matching
papers.summary: Proposed E2I-Flow, an EEG-to-image reconstruction framework combining a stationary-wavelet frequency branch and temporal-mixing branch with bidirectional cross-attention and adaptive fusion, aligned to image embeddings via contrastive and MSE losses, then used as conditioning for a Transformer-based conditional flow-matching image generator. It achieved strong zero-shot EEG-to-image retrieval and improved reconstruction performance over several state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: A high robustness decoding technique for ultrasound modulated electroencephalogram.
papers.summary: Developed a robust decoding algorithm for ultrasound-modulated EEG based on ultrasound pulse repetition frequency and introduced the acoustoelectric modulation ratio (AMR) to classify coupling conditions. Across simulations, phantoms, and human SSVEP data from 10 volunteers, the algorithm achieved 0.79 mm encoding spatial resolution and outperformed four traditional methods under weak, moderate, and over-modulation conditions (average decoding correlations 0.84-0.90).

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Graph Analysis Reveals Enhanced Alpha-Band Integration in High-IQ Individuals: The MENSA-Connect Project.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state 64-channel EEG functional connectivity (lagged linear coherence) between 29 MENSA high-IQ participants and 20 controls using sLORETA-based graph theory. High-IQ individuals showed shorter alpha-band characteristic path length (greater global integration) and higher beta-band clustering coefficient with longer path length (greater local specialization), with no group differences in small-worldness across bands.

papers.title: Profound EEG Suppression Does Not Justify Discontinuation of Anesthesia and Analgesia.
papers.summary: Argues that profound EEG suppression during anesthesia does not justify discontinuing anesthesia and analgesia, addressing the interpretation of burst-suppression and suppressed EEG as a signal for reducing anesthetic delivery.

papers.title: Matching Corticospinal and Cortical Excitability along the motor cortex: TMS-EMG-EEG study
papers.summary: Combined TMS with EMG and EEG in 24 subjects to relate cortical excitability thresholds (CETs, EEG) to resting motor thresholds (RMTs, EMG) at hand, arm, and leg hotspots along M1. RMTs and CETs were strongly correlated and both increased from hand to arm to leg, CETs were generally lower than RMTs, and within-subject CET-RMT differences occurred at all sites, increasing from hand to leg.

papers.title: In-person UCLA-PEERS® program for adolescents with autism spectrum disorder in Italy: study protocol for a pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial with pragmatic features and exploratory EEG markers of treatment response.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a two-arm pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial comparing in-person Italian UCLA-PEERS® against treatment as usual in 36 adolescents with level 1 autism spectrum disorder, with feasibility measures as the primary focus and the QSQ-R social functioning measure as prespecified principal clinical outcome. It also plans to derive baseline N400 congruency effects from EEG during a gesture-word integration task to explore associations with treatment response.

papers.title: Reducing the Risk of Gradient Induced EEG Hardware Heating During Simultaneous EEG-fMRI
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that placing EEG amplifiers and powerpacks within the MRI bore during simultaneous EEG-fMRI creates significant gradient-induced heating risk at 3T and 7T, which can be mitigated by reducing gradient slew rate (e.g., to 61 T/m/s at 7T) or increasing the distance between hardware and magnet isocentre by 30 cm.

papers.title: Multimodal characterization of putative pan-inhibitory viral constructs in macaque monkeys
papers.summary: The authors characterized three Dlx5-6-derived pan-inhibitory viral constructs in seven rhesus macaques using in vivo electrophysiology, in vitro slice electrophysiology, and immunohistochemistry, finding transgene expression restricted to inhibitory neurons in 81-97% of cells but only 32-64% of local GABAergic neurons, with uneven subtype coverage (strong in parvalbumin-positive, sparse in calbindin-positive, minimal in calretinin-positive interneurons). A DLX2.0-ChrimsonR construct supported effective in vivo optotagging, whereas h56D-bReaChES most effectively suppressed neural activity.

papers.title: Disambiguation of two-tone images aligns object representations in the EEG
papers.summary: Recorded EEG in 17 healthy participants to two-tone images before and after disambiguation via corresponding photographs, dissociating learned image concepts from physical image features. After disambiguation, EEG responses to two-tone images became more similar to those of their photo counterparts, emerging around 100 ms and peaking at 350 ms, with no evidence of generalization to semantic category and alignment only after explicit visual disambiguation.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted chemometric analysis of salivary ATR-FTIR spectra for the diagnosis of oral submucous fibrosis.
papers.summary: This study analyzed salivary ATR-FTIR spectra from 450 participants (150 oral submucous fibrosis, 150 with adverse oral habits, 150 controls) using PCA and machine learning classifiers with stratified 10-fold cross-validation, where XGBoost achieved accuracies of 90.62% for Normal versus Habit, 97.67% for Normal versus OSMF, and 91.30% for three-class classification. In an independent 90-participant validation cohort, accuracy was 80.0% for OSMF versus Normal and 71.7% for Habit versus Normal.

papers.title: Dual-modal synaptic operation in a van der Waals heterostructure for emotion-inspired neuromorphic processing.
papers.summary: Fabricated bimodally modulated artificial synapses from a van der Waals-stacked GQD/MoS2 heterostructure that integrate dopamine (1-5 nM) and optical stimuli, showing synergistic postsynaptic current enhancement and stable plasticity over 1000 s. Device-informed simulations reached 73.4% accuracy on facial emotion recognition (FER-2013, CNN) and 76.6% on EEG-inspired PSC temporal-signal classification (SVM).

papers.title: A multimodal optimisation framework for cardiac electrophysiology model personalisation using computed tomography and 12-lead electrocardiogram: Algorithm development and validation.
papers.summary: A multimodal optimization framework combining CT and 12-lead ECG for personalizing cardiac electrophysiology models was tested in six patients, achieving 91.20% mean QRS peak accuracy and reducing average QRS duration error to 3.94 ms (vs. 37.42 ms baseline), with simulations reproducing clinical VT patterns in four patients.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
